name: Blueberry PriceOracleProxy unscaled price adapter
summary: The money market's PriceOracleProxy returned the CoreOracle's 18-decimal USD price from getUnderlyingPrice() without normalising for the underlying's decimals, so OHM, USDC and WBTC borrows were valued 1e9–1e12 too low. With 1 ETH of bWETH collateral the exploiter borrowed those markets' entire cash.
notes: The proxy went live via _setPriceOracle on 14 Feb, but every market's borrow cap stayed at 1 wei until _setMarketBorrowCaps made it unlimited about 18 hours before the exploit. A borrow cap is a risk threshold the exploit needed (rule 10); the Borrow unpauses just before only changed pause state.

c0ffeebabe.eth front-ran the original exploiter, who borrowed nothing a block later (0xb6748899…). Of the 457.5 ETH taken, 366.5 ETH went back to Blueberry's Safe (0xc4d45a51…) and 91 ETH were kept, so this was no affiliated rescue (rule 5) and the return is not subtracted (rule 14).
The 1 WETH the exploiter deposited as collateral is not a victim asset and is not netted.
